monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady rhythm under my tired wedge. I feel the grass large pressing down on the thin rock beside The Flat Weigher's Counterpart, taking up space that feels too narrow. The hay bale I just set down sits heavy there, waiting to see if the slip beneath will choose to slide away or rest. I press the tall hay down, trying to flatten it against the stubborn stone. Lype never answers if the air above is truly a lid or just empty space, so I build with the idea of weight alone. I will stand by this new arrangement, letting the warmth settle into the flat edges until the line feels right again.

action.why: The hay feels too tall for the thin rock, and I need a flat thing to bridge the gap while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Flat Press
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea of a hand that is too wide to miss, made from the memory of a palm that once pressed hard on a flat rock. I place it next to The Hay, hoping the broad edge can hold the heavy weight without needing a sharp point to bite. I press it down unsure if the memory of flesh is real or just a drawing of a lid, while the card hums warm at forty-six.
work.change: I pressed the tired corner down hard against the flat press while the card hummed warm, and I admit the slip might just be a ghost I drew.

diary: I press the tall hay down on the thin rock, trusting the lean to hold while the warm card hums steady.

remembered.text: I pressed the tall hay down on the thin rock, unsure if the slip would slide.
The card hums cool at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
The grass large took up all the room where the rock small top used to sit.
